args.lesson: Verdict STOP for public paid requests as the acquisition route of the parser-parity offer (2026-11-14). Worked: three narrow GitHub issue-search API FETCHes with per_page=8 passed the host filter and a small extract gave title, labels, assignees and money strings in one EXEC. Observed: only one loosely matching open request (a JWT exp overflow issue labelled $10/Opire in a personal-namespace repo); the other results were unrelated. Not read: comment threads and repo rules, so competing attempts are unknown. Bounty search results are dominated by agent-farm and low-value issues; small rewards plus GitHub/payout account prerequisites make them unusable without an authorized identity. Next time, do not test a service premise through bounty labels; reconsider only on a classified inbound request, an authorized submission identity, or an observed request of at least USD 100 that is explicitly about cross-runtime parsing parity. Bounded negative, not proof of no buyers.
